body.x: Cam.ON, a smart camera accessary brand, showcased a new conceptual smartphone lens system at “CES (Consumer Electronic Show) 2016”, the world’s largest IT electronics and tech exhibition, which runs for four days from Wednesday the 6th to Saturday the 9th in Las Vegas.

“Cam.ON” is a camera system for smartphones, and it consists of a smartphone case, four lenses (wide angle, telephoto, ultra-wide angle, and fisheye and micro lenses), an LED strobe (an LED flash), and a holder. Users can take clear and vivid photos with this product, as it minimizes chromatic aberration and light concentration with a low-dispersion lens utilized for DSLR cameras.

The lenses can be changed according to shooting conditions. Unlike regular smartphone cameras, this product has a detachable LED flash, which enables users to take shots and selfies even in dark conditions. The product can transmit data via Bluetooth, and 42 different moods can be produced by adjusting the brightness of the white and yellow LED flash. This can be achieved through Cam.ON’s app for iOS and Android.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), CES 2016 is the world's largest exhibition to see the latest global trends in electronics and IT industry in one spot.

AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES for 11 years to introduce the new technologies and products. After the local coverage and research, AVING News will hold 'CES 2016 Review Conference' in AVING Studio, Korea on January 28th.
